title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends Seven Mumbai Eateries Over Food Safety Violations
excerpt: Raids on October 23-24 found unhygienic kitchens, unauthorised colours and missing handler medical certificates at outlets from Lower Parel to Andheri West, in a statewide drive that seized Rs 1.56 crore of food stock.
body:
• Maharashtra's FDA suspended licences or registrations of seven Mumbai eateries after inspections on October 23 and 24 found unhygienic kitchens, poor drainage and improper storage of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food.
  • The seven are Mumbai Darbar in Lower Parel, Ottoman Cafe and Bharat Canteen in Andheri West, Chacha Eagle Kulfi Falooda in Jogeshwari West, Green Turtle Hospitality in Oshiwara, Atul Tiffin in Byculla and P. B. Enterprises in Sewri West.
  • Inspectors also cited unauthorised food colours and missing medical certificates for food handlers — violations of Schedule 4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration) Regulations, 2011.
  • The wider statewide drive seized 43.56 tonnes of food stock and 719.2 litres of milk and ghee worth about Rs 1.56 crore; if you eat out in Mumbai, check that an outlet's FSSAI licence is displayed and current before ordering.

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration has suspended the licences or registrations of seven Mumbai food establishments after raids on October 23 and 24 found kitchens and storage practices in breach of food safety law. The action, led by FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, was part of a statewide enforcement drive ahead of Diwali, according to reporting summarising the FDA order.

Which Eateries Were Named

The seven establishments are Mumbai Darbar Family Restaurant in Lower Parel, Ottoman Cafe in Andheri West, Chacha Eagle Kulfi Falooda in Jogeshwari West, Bharat Canteen in Andheri West, Green Turtle Hospitality in Oshiwara, Atul Tiffin in Byculla and P. B. Enterprises in Sewri West. A suspended licence means an outlet cannot legally operate until the violations are corrected and the suspension is lifted.

What Inspectors Found

Inspectors reported unhygienic kitchens and drainage systems in poor condition, improper storage of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, use of unauthorised food colours, and the absence of medical certificates for food handlers. Each establishment was found in violation of Schedule 4 of the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration) Regulations, 2011, which sets conditions for hygiene, storage and personnel. Unauthorised colours matter because food colouring is permitted in India only for certain categories and quantities, and missing medical certificates mean a handler with an undiagnosed infection could contaminate meals across a shift.

A Statewide Sweep, Not Just Restaurants

The Mumbai suspensions sat inside a much larger drive. As Trak.in reported, the FDA seized about 43.56 tonnes of food products across Maharashtra and destroyed 564 litres of milk in Mumbai, with the seized stock, milk and ghee valued at around Rs 1.56 crore. Inspections at dairies and milk sellers in Govandi, Mankhurd, Antop Hill, Chembur, Dharavi and Mahim on October 23 and 24 led to samples being taken for laboratory testing. At Sagar Milk Centre in Antop Hill, officials destroyed 250 litres of pasteurised toned milk worth Rs 11,625 because it was stored and sold in plastic bags and cans contrary to prescribed requirements.

Division-level seizures underline the spread: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar recorded 26.84 tonnes worth about Rs 64 lakh, Konkan 9.99 tonnes worth Rs 53.55 lakh, Nashik 4,069 kg and 62.2 litres of ghee worth Rs 8.25 lakh, and Pune 2.11 tonnes worth Rs 7.93 lakh. The products were suspected to be adulterated, substandard or incorrectly labelled.

What This Means for Diners

For Mumbai residents — and for diaspora families visiting the city during the festive season — the practical lesson is to buy milk and perishables from reliable sellers and check packaging, storage and expiry information. The FDA has said enforcement will continue against establishments that violate prescribed standards. Whether the seven suspended outlets reopen will depend on correcting the Schedule 4 violations and passing re-inspection.
